reviewer: claude-opus-5 acting as the joshi pump-discovery deputy, autonomously, without Ember present
rationale: PROMOTED for /coins/search-unrestricted, the route that carries the one field this lane went looking for. WHY A ROW PROJECTION AND NOT A DOCUMENT FINGERPRINT. schema_fingerprint collapses every array element onto the single pointer $/*, so a page's digest is the UNION of the key sets of whichever coins happened to land in it. Eleven reads of /coins on 2026-08-22 produced EIGHT distinct fingerprints; two byte-identical requests ninety-seven seconds apart differed by exactly cto_address, cto_username and cto_profile_image because one page contained a coin with a community takeover recorded and the other did not. That gate reports on which coins arrived, not on whether the provider changed anything, so it would admit about one read in eight and label the other seven provider drift. This review narrows instead: every row must carry the required leaves in the reviewed wire type, a row may carry the optional leaves, and ANY other leaf refuses the page rather than being silently projected away. Silent projection is exactly how ath_market_cap and volume_1h_usd went missing from three routes for three days without one test going red. The optional set is CLOSED: adding to it is a review act performed by a person writing down what they looked at, never an inference from a body that happened to arrive. The whole-document fingerprint is still recorded on every decision as a drift signal; it simply decides nothing. REVIEWED MATERIAL, as v1 first wrote it down: 7 live response bodies and 355 rows, all fetched 2026-08-22 through the bounded source-edge client. leaf lines present on every one of those 355 rows were required and are required here; 42 more appeared on some rows and not others and are the closed optional set. A leaf line is `pointer:wire-type`, so a field that legitimately arrives under two types is two lines and a nullable field is one line plus its `:null`; there is no way to write down `any type`. HOLDOUT: built from seven bodies fetched between 03:22Z and 03:26Z, then checked against a body fetched at 03:34Z that contributed nothing to it. That later page promoted. MEASURED SEMANTICS. Bare top-level JSON array of the same coin record as /coins, plus volume_1h_usd, a realised one-hour USD volume that exists NOWHERE ELSE in this catalog, and plus a nested `mayhem` object whose leaves are $/mayhem/state, $/mayhem/mode and $/mayhem/pause_reason — the only nested structure on any coin row measured. ORDERING: rows arrive STRICTLY DESCENDING by volume_1h_usd, verified monotone across all 70 rows for searchTerm=cat and again for searchTerm=a, and verified to continue correctly across an offset page whose highest volume, 1169 USD, sat below the previous page's lowest, 1286 USD. It is a live-volume leaderboard filtered by a term, whatever its path says. THE TERM IS LOAD-BEARING, AND A CORRECTION THIS REVIEWER OWES: with searchTerm omitted, and again with it empty, the returned rows carry NO volume_1h_usd KEY AT ALL — 0 of 20 rows on each of two such pages. An earlier note of mine recorded those rows as having volume_1h_usd of exactly zero. That was my own readout defaulting an absent field to 0, which is precisely the fabrication this codebase exists to refuse, and it is why volume_1h_usd is an OPTIONAL leaf here rather than a required one. Those no-term pages are ordered ASCENDING by market cap and are long-dead coins. This route therefore cannot enumerate a global active universe in one call; any sweep of terms that approximates one is a biased sample of whatever those terms matched. ALSO OPTIONAL AND SURPRISING: virtual_sol_reserves, virtual_token_reserves, virtual_quote_reserves, real_token_reserves and total_supply each went missing on some rows — 65 of 70 rows carried the reserve quartet on one page — so a coin row here may carry no curve state whatsoever. limit=100 returned 100 rows, where the sibling /coins silently clamps to 70; caps are measured per route and never inherited. volume_1h_usd is a provider aggregate over a window whose edges this catalog cannot see, so it can never be reconciled against trades this codebase holds. This review was made by an agent, not by Ember. AMENDED 2026-08-22 04:08Z, v1 -> v2, ON EVIDENCE AND NOT ON INFERENCE. v1 refused all three flow pages of the first live sweep — acquisitions ...1787371709209753-0a13bea5d2edca435ac6fe58745eaf0b, ...1787371710409593-aef0ca244077930c39b61c00be6f7dfc and ...1787371711584192-d3722408c89a6d11ab80bf64d29f2f52 — each because a row carried $/mayhem/complete_reason:string, a nested leaf no reviewer had looked at. Reading those retained bodies shows it beside the mayhem state: {"state":"completed","mode":"auto","complete_reason":"zero_base_amount"} and "sell_zero_amount". A second leaf, $/tokenized_agent:boolean, appeared on later bodies for the same reason. Both are added to the CLOSED optional set here, and the listing below is recomputed over 12 bodies and 665 rows including those three. That is the whole workflow this gate is for: it fails closed on a field nobody has read, names the row and the leaf, and a person then writes down what they looked at. Nothing was widened to a shape that has not been seen. AMENDED AGAIN, v2 -> v3, AND THIS TIME THE PRINCIPLE CHANGED RATHER THAN THE OBSERVATIONS. Three separate live pages refused within minutes of v1 shipping, each on a genuinely unobserved provider fact: a coin created with NO metadata at all (mint 3E3bEpbFDxyBy6KDqdBKRAFiLZTn49mG19KAMW1jpump, name "NA") carrying no image_uri; a nested $/mayhem/complete_reason no reviewer had read, seen as {"state":"completed","mode":"auto","complete_reason":"zero_base_amount"}; and a search row for a coin that has never traded, carrying no last_trade_timestamp. Each refusal was correct and each was cheap to resolve, but the pattern showed the required set was being computed wrongly: it was every leaf seen on every row, INCLUDING leaves this crate never reads. Requiring an unread field buys nothing — its absence cannot harm any consumer — and costs a refusal every time the provider omits it on a rare row, which is how a fail-closed gate becomes noise that a tired reader learns to wave through. From v3 the required set is scoped to EXACTLY the projection the normalizer reads, and RowProjectionReviewV1::validate now REFUSES any review that requires a leaf outside that projection. Everything else the provider sends is still in the CLOSED optional set, so an unreviewed leaf still refuses the page: the anti-silent-drop rule is untouched. What changed is that a required-leaf refusal now means a field this codebase actually consumes went missing, which is a fact worth stopping for. A NOTE FOR WHOEVER OPERATES THIS. The required set is an EMPIRICAL claim — leaves present on every row of every body looked at so far — and it will occasionally be refuted by a rarer row. Early operation should expect refusals, and a refusal is a finding rather than a fault: read the named row in the retained bytes, decide whether the leaf really is optional, and amend. It must never be resolved by widening to a shape nobody has read. v3 leaf listing recomputed over 14 live bodies and 865 rows: 24 required, every one of them a field the normalizer reads, and 49 optional. Leaves present on every row but never read by this crate — hide_banner, image_uri, livestream_ban_expiry, show_name — are optional here for that reason and not because they were seen missing.
